title: eshyra-c7sx PR #462 review fixes (per-period termination, sibling timers, chronological ordering)
description:
Fix the three P1 findings from the PR #462 review of the item reset/timer executor (parent bead eshyra-c7sx; the executor lives in packages/core/src/state/itemResetExecutor.ts, integrated on branch eshyra-c7sx). All three were verified against head commit 9222f5d. Read the PR's inline comments if helpful: `gh api repos/jbongaarts/eshyra/pulls/462/comments`.

## Finding 1 — per-period resets never stop at maximum (itemResetExecutor.ts ~650, resetAnchoredItem per-period branch)

The while-loop unconditionally installs the next `availableAt` anchor, so a fully restored per-period economy (winged-boots) keeps firing `applyReset` at every later period crossing forever: `restored: 0` evidence entries, pointless state writes, and unbounded evidence growth on large advances. Fix: chain periods only while `remaining < maximum`; when the economy reaches (or already has) its maximum, clear `availableAt` and stop. A subsequent spend re-anchors it (useItem already overwrites availableAt on every spend). Regression: fill the economy, advance another period, assert no new evidence and `availableAt === undefined`; then spend again and assert the anchor is re-established.

## Finding 2 — sibling timers survive leaving their source state (itemResetExecutor.ts ~747, resolveTimers)

`remainingTimers = pending.filter(c => c !== timer)` removes only the fired timer. With two outgoing timer transitions from the same state, the sibling survives after `machineState` changes; when it comes due the executor throws (`timer.from !== state.machineState`) — and because this runs inside advanceWorldTime's transaction, ALL campaign time advancement is permanently blocked for that item's campaign. It also contradicts reconcileItemStateTimers's documented contract ("timers from the state being left are cancelled"). Fix: drop every pending timer whose `from === timer.from` before adding the entered state's newly scheduled timers. Regression: a state with two outgoing timers (1 min and 5 min); advance 1 minute — earlier wins, sibling cancelled; advance 5 more minutes — no throw, no stale transition.

## Finding 3 — clock events execute out of chronological order (itemResetExecutor.ts ~893, resolveDueItemClockEvents)

Current sequence per item: all dawn crossings, then all dusks, then anchored resets, then timers. Consequences: an item whose timer destroys it at minute 1 still receives a dawn recharge at minute 360 first (consuming RNG, emitting evidence for an item that should already be gone); multi-day dawn/dusk crossings are applied out of order; an anchored deadline earlier than an already-applied dawn can move `lastReset` backward. Fix: per item, apply due events in a unified chronological order — repeatedly select the earliest due event among (next unapplied dawn crossing, next dusk crossing, each economy's next anchored/per-period due, earliest pending timer deadline), apply it, and continue until nothing is due at or before `elapsedMinutes`; timer-driven destruction terminates that item's processing. Pick a deterministic tie-breaker for equal minutes (recommend: timers before resets, then a stable secondary key like economy id) and document it in docs/item-reset-executor.md. Keep evidence arrays in applied order. Regressions: destruction-at-minute-1 + dawn-charges item advanced past dawn (no reset evidence, inventory gone); a two-day advance asserting dawn/dusk evidence strictly ordered by boundary minute.

## Constraints

- Preserve all existing behavior otherwise: fail-closed rules, evidence shapes, lastReset/availableAt semantics, and the 16 existing tests (adjust only where an assertion encodes the buggy ordering).
- All state writes stay on the validateItemStateForRecord/writeItemState path.
- Update docs/item-reset-executor.md where semantics change (per-period termination, chronological ordering, tie-breaker).
- `npm run verify:worktree` fully green before commit; commit on this worktree's branch.
- Record your completion report with `bd update <this-bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this-bead>`. Never close or modify eshyra-c7sx; never touch files outside this worktree.
notes: Fixed all three PR #462 P1 findings plus two fixes lost to the branch reset, in commit b00e4d5 on eshyra-c7sx (pushed as a fast-forward, no history rewrite). (1) per-period economies re-anchor only while below maximum; (2) firing a timer cancels every timer owned by the state being left; (3) resolveItemTimeline applies dawn/dusk, anchored, and timer events in chronological order per item, ties running timers first. Restored: anchored resets record their due minute; pendingTerminal completes only when the entered state has no outgoing transition. Also rejects a timer that would expire no later than the transition entering its state (previously an infinite loop inside the advance transaction). Five new regressions all verified to fail against the pre-fix executor. Full verify:worktree green: 4687 passed / 19 skipped.
close_reason: Fixed in b00e4d5; replies posted to all three PR #462 review threads
